title: PLC diagnostics
summary: Controllers and modules report problems through LEDs, a diagnostic buffer, channel status and quality information. Reading them first saves hours of guessing.

sections.heading: Where diagnostic information lives
sections.body:
- **LEDs** on CPU and modules: RUN/STOP, ERROR, MAINT, per-channel status.
- **Diagnostic buffer**: a time-stamped list of incoming and outgoing events (module missing, wire break, CPU stop with cause).
- **Channel quality / status**: analog values with overflow or wire-break flags.
- **Communication status**: connection timeouts, exception codes, link state.

sections.heading: Incoming and outgoing
sections.body: A diagnostic event is **incoming** when the problem appears and **outgoing** when it disappears. A list that shows a wire break going and coming every few seconds points to a loose terminal.

sections.heading: Diagnostics in PLC Lab
sections.body: The Diagnostics tab shows the CPU diagnostic buffer and active process alarms. The hardware view shows module status, LEDs, channel values and quality, and offers a multimeter. Network faults appear as connection diagnostics and in the network message list.
